摘.meaning: A lighthouse keeper can't reach the cherries on the tree below her cliff. Each night, by the glow of a <part>hanging lantern</part>, she lowers a tiny <part>anchor</part> on a fishing line, snags one stalk and reels it up. One cherry at a time is how she likes to <kanji>pluck</kanji>.
摘.on: She sends her sister a <sound>tex</sound>t message with a photo of every cherry.
摘.kun: When a cherry falls on her nose she sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and a <sound>moo</sound>se below catches it.

鑑.meaning: A museum guard has one job: to <part>oversee</part> a single glass case. Inside, pinned on velvet, is a beetle of solid <part>gold</part>, the only one ever found. He hasn't blinked in years, and some nights it winks back. Scientists fly in just to peer at the <kanji>specimen</kanji>.
鑑.on: Each visitor leaves a pink <sound>car</sound>nation by the case.
鑑.kun: Its label is written in <sound>car</sound>nation-pink ink, beside a clove of <sound>ga</sound>rlic to keep the moths away.

疾.meaning: Rain drips through a <part>leaky shed</part> where an old man plays darts alone. A drip falls, he throws a <part>dart</part> and pins it to the wall before it hits the floor. Then the next, and the next. His arm is a blur. Nothing moves so <kanji>rapidly</kanji>.
疾.on: He hangs a bed <sound>shee</sound>t on the wall to catch the darts.
疾.kun: His cat watches from a little <sound>hu</sound>t of boxes, batting a ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn just as fast.

禅.meaning: A street <part>lamppost</part> grows tired of the city's noise. It stops flickering, stops buzzing, and makes its whole life <part>simple</part>: one steady light, no thoughts. Moths land on it and fall asleep, and even the pigeons whisper. The lamppost has found <kanji>Zen</kanji>.
禅.on: Each night it lights a tiny <sound>zen</sound> garden at its foot, the sand raked into circles.
禅.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p dozes under it, a yu<sound>zu</sound> rolls by without a bump, and a <sound>ca</sound>rp in the gutter doesn't splash: all quiet.

鼓.meaning: A beaver finds an old <part>drum</part> washed down the river. Having no sticks, she snaps a <part>branch</part> off an alder and starts thumping. Every animal in the valley comes to dance on the dam. She gives up building for good and spends her days on the <kanji>drum</kanji>.
鼓.on: A sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala keeps time by thumping its tail on a log.
鼓.kun: The dust makes her sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and a yu<sound>zu</sound> bounces off the drum onto a <sound>mee</sound>rkat's head.

妃.meaning: A <part>woman</part> who charms snakes at the fair plays her flute, and a <part>cobra</part> rises from the basket, coils round her head and spreads its hood like a jewelled crown. The crowd bows without knowing why. For that one tune, she's a <kanji>queen</kanji>.
妃.on: She bows back and wobbles on one tall <sound>hee</sound>l.
妃.kun: Her purse holds a gold <sound>key</sound>, a <sound>sa</sound>rdine for the snake and a second <sound>key</sound> for the basket.

戯.meaning: A bored knight stands guard over a <part>void</part>, a great empty hole where the castle used to be. Nobody's coming, so he plants his <part>spear</part>, swings round it like a dancer and turns cartwheels by the edge. The crows join in. On duty, he can't help but <kanji>frolic</kanji>.
戯.on: The rusty <sound>gear</sound> in his visor whirs as he spins.
戯.kun: He lands in a <sound>tu</sound>b of rainwater, yells '<sound>Wah</sound>!', and a <sound>moo</sound>se laughs at him.
